Strix Halo (8060S / gfx1151), Qwen-3.8-27B @ Q8 and Q6 UD v3, up to 256K ctx, llama.cpp, DFlash2, vision, real workloads quality and steady performances, optimized recipes, ...
Resources

Hi fellows fully-local halos,

after manually following existing guides, I decided to build an LLM API endpoint installation and optimization guide that works even when autonomously followed by my pi agent, so I can install/experiment/reinstall easily and without babysitting.

Q8 is my default citizen, options for Q6 and Q5. Recipes: Quality (Q8), Balanced (Q6), Speed (Q5), Vision (Q8). All with Unsloth Dynamic Quants 3.0, DFlash2 (except vision). Scripts for download the right LLMs, interactive testing, systemd `--user` install, adaptive quality and performances optimization.

Repo: https://github.com/PieBru/Qwen-3.8-27B_Strix-Halo_gfx1151

Humans architected, verified, sealed. AI assistants built and wrote all the delivered stuff, built with pi and Qwen-3.8-27B.

Piero

P.S.: constructive proposals and PR are welcome.

P.P.S.: no speed races, please. IMO speed is useful, but quality is fundamental - one subtle bug fewer or a better codebase always pays for itself in wall-time gained.

This is why in the post I wrote "Humans architected, verified, sealed. AI assistants built and wrote all the delivered stuff, built with pi and Qwen-3.8-27B."

Your agent ran into vk::DeviceLostError after 128k context right?

PieBru
•
4h ago

Yes, at ~160k filling (allocating works up to 256k) and thanks for spotting that possible upstream bug (Vulkan?). Anyway, very bad wording in the README, updated now.

I verified and used all ctx allocations up to 256k, they all work. The tg speed depends on the filled context, not the allocated context, so allocating 256k costs only RAM (with 128GB RAM it doesn't hurt me). The vulkan issue (bug?) is when the prefill reaches ~160k.

I used to set the ctx to 128k because in my everyday usage (pi + ponytail) it's large enough for the agent workloads, at the same time small enough to avoid most large context problems.

Weeks ago, pi agent was auto-compacting the context at the end of a "phase" (no further prompts queued) and it often overflowed past my 128k setting, this is why I was using 256k, but observed the Vulkan bug at ~160k. meanwhile, pi agent probably fixed that bug, because now it compacts before reaching the max context threshold.

Corrected the README, as my pi verified: "Now TL;DR and body say the same thing: 256k of window, ~128k of content — the margin rule (soft 100k < fence 128k < crash ~160k) stays intact underneath."
